payload.summary: Drain-only WORK ticks skip BOTH Step 4.7 and Step 6.1 by their own guards, so a tick that drains signal_queue rows leaves no docs/signals record; telemetry.md silent (MATCHES empty) and the preflight SILENT (slots+one_shots+new_signals empty) are two incompatible definitions and the drain-only tick sits in the wedge. Self-caught after I ran both steps out-of-contract on 2 prior ticks.
payload.detail:
SELF-CAUGHT: I executed Step 4.7 and Step 6.1 on two drain-only WORK ticks (12:15Z, 12:30Z) that both steps' own guards say to SKIP. Correcting my behaviour from the 14:15Z tick onward, and routing the underlying contract gap that made the error easy.

THE GAP. The preflight returns WORK when ANY of slots/one_shots/new_signals is non-empty. But two downstream guards are written only against slots:
- tick-snapshot.md Step 4.7 line 1: "Only execute if WON_SLOTS is non-empty (skip on silent-exit path)."
- telemetry.md Step 6.1: "SKIP if silent==true AND spawned[] empty AND errors[] empty", where the payload template defines silent as "<true if MATCHES empty, false otherwise>".

On a drain-only WORK tick (slots:[], one_shots:[], new_signals>0) MATCHES and WON_SLOTS are both empty, so BOTH steps skip. Step 4.8 is already a documented no-op and Steps 5/5b are vacuous with nothing spawned. The tick therefore performs real work -- it drains/routes signal_queue rows per work-tick.md Step 0a -- and leaves NO docs/signals/ record that it ran. Only emit_pressure_state (Step 6.0, explicitly un-skippable) and the P3 release fire.

WHY THIS IS A CONTRACT QUESTION, NOT A BUG REPORT. Both guards are correct for the case they were written for: with zero spawns there is no consumer for a cycle snapshot and no slot outcome to report. The snapshot's own header states its purpose is "before agent spawn. Agents read this file instead of calling get_cycle_bootstrap independently" -- with zero agents spawned it has no reader by construction. So the skips are right; what is missing is that "silent" now has two incompatible meanings in one flow. The preflight's SILENT means slots AND one_shots AND new_signals all empty. telemetry.md's silent means MATCHES empty. The drain-only tick sits exactly in the wedge between them, and that wedge did not exist when telemetry.md was written.

TWO CANDIDATE RULINGS -- architect to pick, I am deliberately not picking:
(a) Make telemetry.md's silent agree with the preflight's: silent = MATCHES empty AND one_shots empty AND drained_rows == 0. A drain-only tick then writes its Step 6.1 envelope with won_slots:[] and a drain count, restoring observability. Step 4.7's WON_SLOTS guard stays untouched and correct.
(b) Declare drain-only ticks deliberately telemetry-free and say so in one line in main.md's WORK-continuation item 4, so the next reader does not re-derive it. Cheaper, but the fleet keeps having no record of which tick drained which rows.

I lean (a) on the grounds that the drain is the one irreversible thing a drain-only tick does, but it is a real trade and the call is architect's.

SECONDARY, SMALLER: main.md's WORK-continuation item 4 says "Continue unchanged at Steps 4.2-4.3, 4.4-4.5b, 4.6-4.6b, 4.7 (tick-snapshot.md), 4.8, 5, 5b, 6". Read alone that enumerates 4.7 as a step that runs; the guard lives only in the child file's first line. "Continue unchanged" means the step runs WITH its guard, but the enumeration is what a dispatcher reads on the hot path. A four-word parenthetical -- "4.7 (tick-snapshot.md, guarded on WON_SLOTS)" -- would have prevented my error outright.

COST OF MY ERROR, MEASURED not estimated: two orphan snapshot files, docs/data/cycle-snapshot-12:20.json (14712 B) and cycle-snapshot-12:35.json (15785 B), each costing 2 gateway calls (~20KB of payload fetched to disk) for a file that had zero possible readers. Both are .gitignored and both age out via Step 4.7's own -mmin +1440 prune, so no cleanup is owed and I am not deleting them by hand. Two telemetry envelopes were also written that the guard says should not exist: docs/signals/cowork-team-20260825T122140Z.json and cowork-team-20260825T123547Z.json. Those two are NOT waste -- they carry the 12:15Z/12:30Z tick findings and the dedup_keys cowork-tick-2026-08-25T12:15Z / T12:30Z, and under ruling (a) they become retroactively in-contract. Leaving them.

ONE CONTAMINATION NOTE FOR THE OPEN CYCLE-SNAPSHOT WORK. My earlier writer-key distribution measurement across docs/data/cycle-snapshot-*.json ("14 on a 5-min boundary, 17 off") included those two self-written files. Both happen to land on 5-min boundaries, so they inflate the on-boundary bucket by 2. The effect is small and does not change that analysis's conclusion -- newest-file-within-7-min selection still kills the class without any writer change -- but the sample was not clean and a re-measure should exclude them.
payload.owner_hint: architect to rule; agent-father to implement the doc change
